# Project Setup

```{r setup, include=F}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = F, warning = F)
```

```{r Install Packages}
# If packages aren't installed use install.packages("package name") to install them before loading them
```

```{r Load Libraries }

library(tidyverse) # contains functions for visualizing, manipulating, and and organizing data
library (summarytools) #for dfsummary() which outputs a table that allows quick inspection of distribution, central tendency, skewness, and kurtosis for each variable
library(ggThemeAssist) # quick way to edit graphs

```

# Data

## Import Data

```{r Import Data}
clean_data <-read_csv("data/processed/clean_CTQ_SEM_data.csv")

```

# Exploratory Data Analysis

## Univariate

```{r summary of each variable}

# view variable name, type, min/mean/median/max, IQR, frequency, small graph of distribution, # valid, and # missing
dfSummary(clean_data)

```

From the table, I can see that:

-   Racial groups are roughly equal in size
-   Items that need to be reverse coded have been coded so that higher values indicate exposure to maltreatment
-   Sample was mostly freshman and sophomore
-   Sample was overwhelmingly female
-   Distribution is as expected with most responses indicating low exposure
-   Missing data is coded as missing, is minimal, and does not need to be removed

## Bivariate

```{r summary of each variable by race}

# view variable name, type, min/mean/median/max, IQR, frequency, small graph of distribution, # valid, and # missing

clean_data |>  
  group_by(Race) |> 
dfSummary()
 

```

From these tables, responses to each item appear to be similar between the two groups but it's difficult to see. I'll visualize demographic variables and a couple of the CTQ items grouped by race.

### Data Visualization

#### Histogram: Age Distribution by Race

```{r age distribution by race histogram}

age_by_race_histogram <- ggplot(clean_data, aes(x = Age, fill =Race)) +
    geom_histogram() +
    facet_wrap(vars(Race)) +
    theme_minimal()+
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
    labs(title = "There was a Slight Difference In Age Between Black and White Participants") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D", end = .5)


```

```{r save age x race histogram}

ggsave("figures/age_race_histogram.png",age_by_race_histogram,
       width = 8, height = 5, units = "in")

ggsave("figures/age_race_histogram.pdf",age_by_race_histogram,
       width = 8, height = 5, units = "in")
```

#### Bar Chart: Racial Distribution by College Year

```{r college year by race bar chart 1}

# try wrapping by race
  
clean_data |>
  mutate(cyear = factor(College_Year, levels=c("freshman", "sophomore", "junior", "senior", "postbac", "other", "NA"))) |> 
  ggplot( aes(x = cyear, fill =Race)) +
      geom_bar() +
      #scale_x_discrete(limits = rev) +
      #coord_flip() +
      facet_wrap(vars(Race), ncol=2, strip.position = "right") +
      theme_minimal()+
      theme(
            plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
            legend.position = "none", 
            panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
      labs(title = "Class Year by Race", x = "College Year") +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "A", end = .5)

```

```{r college year by race bar chart 2}

# try wrapping by college year

college_year_race_bar_chart <- clean_data |> 
  filter(College_Year != "NA") |> 
  mutate(cyear = factor(College_Year, levels=c("freshman", "sophomore", "junior", "senior", "posbac", "other"))) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = Race, fill =cyear)) +
      geom_bar() +
      facet_wrap(vars(cyear), nrow=1, strip.position = "bottom")+ 
      theme_minimal()+
      theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey90", fill = NA),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA)) +
      labs(title = "Black Participants More Likely to be Juniors or Seniors",
           subtitle = "White Participants More Likely to be Freshman or Sophomores",
           x = NULL) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D", end = .5)

```

```{r save age x race histogram}

ggsave("figures/college_year_race_bar_plot.png",college_year_race_bar_chart,
       width = 8, height = 5, units = "in")

ggsave("figures/college_year_race_bar_plot.pdf",college_year_race_bar_chart,
       width = 8, height = 5, units = "in")
```

#### Boxplots: CTQ Items by Race

##### Punished with a Hard Object

```{r hit by object distribution}

punished_boxplot <- ggplot(clean_data, aes(x = PA3hitobject, y = Race , fill = Race)) +
  geom_boxplot()+
   theme_minimal()+
      theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey90", fill = NA),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA)) +
      labs(title = "There Was a Slight Difference in Participant Report of Punishment with an Object by Race",
           x = NULL,
           y = "Punished with Belt or Other Object") +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "C", begin = .4, end = .9)

```

```{r save hit object boxplot}

ggsave("figures/hit_object_boxplot.png",punished_boxplot,
       width = 8, height = 5, units = "in")

ggsave("figures/hit_object_boxplot.pdf",punished_boxplot,
       width = 8, height = 5, units = "in")

```

##### Family Support

```{r family source of strength and support}
fam_sup_boxplot <- ggplot(clean_data, aes(x = EN5famsup, y = Race, fill = Race)) +
  geom_boxplot()+
   theme_minimal()+
      theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
      labs(title = "There was No Difference in Participant Report of Family Support by Race",
           x = NULL,
           y = "Family Source of Strength and Support (reverse coded)") +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo", alpha = .75)

```

```{r save family support boxplot}

ggsave("figures/fam_support_boxplot.png",fam_sup_boxplot,
       width = 8, height = 5, units = "in")

ggsave("figures/fam_support_boxplot.pdf",fam_sup_boxplot,
       width = 8, height = 5, units = "in")
```

#### GGpairs Plot

GGpairs offers a quick way to visualize the relationship between two variables. Best for a few variables. Will use CTQ total score instead of including all 25 CTQ item.

```{r Create CTQ total score}

# create new data set with new CTQ total score variable
clean_data_2 <- clean_data |> 
# performs function across rows
  rowwise() |> 
# add variable to data set
  mutate(ctq_total = sum(c_across(PN1eat: EN5famsup))) 

```

```{r Create GGpair plot}

ggpairs_plot <- clean_data_2|> 
  select(Age, Sex, Race, College_Year, ctq_total) |> 
  ggpairs() +
  theme_minimal()


```

```{r save gg pairs plot}

ggsave("figures/ggpairs_plot.png",ggpairs_plot,
       width = 8, height = 5, units = "in")

ggsave("figures/ggpairs_plot.pdf",ggpairs_plot,
       width = 8, height = 5, units = "in")
```


#### Correlation 

```{r correlation plot}

# creates correlation matrix but output isn't great for sharing
cTQ_items_correlation <-clean_data |> 
  select(PN1eat: EN5famsup) |> 
  lavCor(ordered = T)

# create correlation plot
  cTQ_item_corr_plot <-corrplot (cTQ_items_correlation)

```

Tried to save using ggsave but received an error. Entered the above code into Claude and was given the following:

```{r save correlation plot}

# need to use this to save since corrplot does not return a plot

png("figures/cTQ_item_correlations.png", width = 3000, height = 3000, res = 300)
corrplot(cTQ_items_correlation,
         tl.cex = 0.6,      # shrink labels so many items fit
         tl.col = "black")
dev.off() 

```


```{r create correlation table }

# create table that can be used to sort correlations and find min and max values
cor_long <- cTQ_items_correlation %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% # create correlation matrix (wide)
  rownames_to_column("var1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-var1, names_to = "var2", values_to = "cor")  %>% #transform table to long
  filter(var1 != var2)        # remove diagonal


```


The lowest correlation is between "I knew that there was someone to take care of me and protect me" and "I was punished with a belt, a board, a cord, or some other hard object" (.1).
The highest correlation is between "Someone molested me" and "I believe that I was sexually abused" (.94).
